subject: Forensics & retention: NovaMed evidence/investigation window and BYOK carveout
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security@novamed.com
Date: 2026-06-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: investigation window + BYOK carveout for NovaMed PII flows

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the earlier demo — following up from NovaMed Security. We're starting our incident response tabletop and need to confirm two things before we move forward with production testing:

1) Evidence / investigation window: for any security incident affecting NovaMed workloads, what is the maximum retainable raw request/response log window you can provide? We need chain-of-custody level artifacts for up to 90 days, but would accept a 30-day short-term option if we can get signed manifests and per-request hashes.

2) BYOK / keystore carveout: can Redwood offer a dedicated key path (BYOK) or escrow for NovaMed so that decryption keys for logs can be separated from Redwood's primary keystore? If not full BYOK, would a short-term ephemeral-keystore + periodic escrow snapshot be acceptable?

I've attached our security questionnaire (see attachment) with some specific asks about audit log granularity and forensics export formats.

Appreciate a quick triage — can you loop in product/engineering so we can align on an approach and timeline. We're targeting a table-top exercise the week of 2026-06-22.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Information Security
NovaMed Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: investigation window + BYOK carveout for NovaMed PII flows

On Thu, Jun 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM irene_choi@redwood.ai wrote:
> High level questions for the team so we can give a single answer back to NovaMed: 

Quick triage notes from eng/ops:

- Signed manifests & per-request hashes: we can generate both. Current exports are JSONL with per-request metadata (timestamp, model, token-count, request-id). We can add a SHA256 per-request hash and sign a daily manifest with our KMS signing key.

- Retention windows: raw request/response storage at 90 days is feasible but will require a dedicated bucket/ingest policy and retention-lifecycle tags. Operational cost estimate: ~0.6–0.9x incremental storage costs for heavy PII customers. We should gate 90d on a reserved-capacity + cost-recovery plan. 30d short-term is low friction and we can do that under existing infra.

- BYOK options: two practical approaches:
  1) Full BYOK for logs: customer-provided CMK in their VPC or HSM. Pros: customer control; Cons: higher ops support, longer onboarding, cross-account key management required.
  2) Ephemeral keystore + periodic escrow snapshot: we rotate ephemeral keys daily and sign a snapshot that we escrow to the customer's KMS (encrypted). This gives a balance between separation and operational simplicity; allows us to keep hot-path performance.

- Forensics/export format: recommend offering both (a) raw JSONL export with hashes and (b) per-request sanitized event export if customer cannot keep raw tokens.

Actionable asks for product/compliance:
- Product: define a UI/API for requesting a signed-manifest export and opt-in retention policies (30d vs 90d).
- Compliance: confirm if escrow snapshots (encrypted for customer CMK) meet chain-of-custody evidence requirements for auditors.

I can scope a PoC for ephemeral-keystore + escrow (2 sprint work) if we get approval.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: investigation window + BYOK carveout for NovaMed PII flows

Elena — thanks for the questionnaire and patience while we triaged. Summary and next steps: 

Summary of options (internal consensus):
- Short-term (fast): 30-day raw logs + signed daily manifests and per-request hashes. No immediate BYOK; use ephemeral-keystore + encrypted escrow snapshots to a customer CMK. Low lift, available under existing infra.
- Mid-term (PoC): ephemeral-keystore + escrow PoC scoped to 2 sprints (engineering). We will produce a signed proof-of-export and sample chain-of-custody document.
- Enterprise option: 90-day raw retention behind reserved capacity + cost-recovery; full BYOK support requires cross-account key provisioning and is a longer onboarding path (legal & infra to approve).

Open questions for NovaMed to confirm before we schedule the tabletop: 
1) For the tabletop, is 30d with signed manifests acceptable to validate forensic playbooks?
2) Do you require full raw request/response bodies during the exercise, or are hashed + redacted event exports sufficient?
3) If you want 90d and/or full BYOK, we'll need a contract addendum and a committed capacity plan.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 30-minute check-in on Tue 2026-06-15 to finalize choices and timeline. (Irene will send a calendar invite)
- Engineering (Marcus): scope PoC and provide a rough estimate by 2026-06-18.
- Compliance (Soojin): confirm whether encrypted escrow snapshots meet evidence requirements by 2026-06-17.

Attaching the retention_matrix.xlsx mapping options and cost/ops impact. I've also opened SEC-4312 in Jira to track the work — please comment if anything is missing.

Thanks all —
